cases.answer: Split before preprocessing. Fit the scaler on training rows only, then transform training and test rows with that fitted scaler; otherwise test features leak into evaluation and make it optimistic.
Test rows must not set the scaling statistics. Split first and fit preprocessing only on training data.
There is no leakage because scaling uses features rather than test labels. Scaling all rows is fine.
required_corrections: Test features can leak through fitted preprocessing statistics; split before fitting.

cases.answer: Accuracy is dominated by legitimate email, so an all-negative filter gets 98% while finding no spam. Precision is true spam among flagged messages; recall is found spam among all actual spam.
The filter is excellent because 98% accuracy means it catches 98% of spam.

cases.answer: The majority baseline hides the minority-class failure. For spam, precision measures reliability of alerts and recall measures coverage of real spam; this classifier has zero recall.
Bagging trains diverse models independently on resampled data and averages them, mainly reducing variance. Boosting trains sequentially to focus later learners on earlier errors and can reduce bias.
Both methods combine many models, so they always do the same thing.
Backpropagation applies the chain rule from the loss backward to compute each parameter gradient. An optimiser then uses those gradients to update weights and reduce loss.
Batch learning retrains from a collected dataset, while online learning updates as new observations arrive. Online learning can adapt to drift but needs monitoring for unstable or bad updates.

Boosting can fit complex patterns by correcting earlier residual errors, but sequential learners can chase noisy labels and overfit. Regularisation, shallow learners and validation help control that risk.
A random forest averages many decorrelated trees. Bootstrap samples and random feature subsets make tree errors less correlated, so averaging reduces variance.

Generalisation is performance on unseen data from the relevant population. Training performance alone can be high because a flexible model memorises noise; a held-out validation or test set estimates generalisation.

Monitor input distributions, prediction distributions and delayed outcome quality where labels arrive. A shift can indicate data drift or a broken pipeline, so alerting should trigger investigation rather than automatic trust.
Persist preprocessing with the trained model and apply the same fitted transformations at inference. Version code, features and data assumptions so a prediction can be reproduced.
If all trees make the same errors, averaging barely helps. Resampling and random feature choices create different trees, allowing averaging to cancel some individual errors.
